title: Vector width compatibility adapter and staged online index migration playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Provide a low-risk, operational playbook and a lightweight compatibility adapter to allow clients and reranking pipelines to tolerate changes in embedding vector width (dimensionality) while we roll out reindexing and quality validations. Focus is on minimizing customer-visible downtime, bounding latency regression for reranking endpoints, and enabling progressive reindex for large corpora.
background: Several product teams intend to upgrade model families that produce embeddings with a different vector width. Full reindex of our largest customers (10M+ docs) is expensive and can take weeks; clients frequently cannot coordinate simultaneous client and server SDK upgrades. Prior internal attempts at naive padding/shrinking introduced unseen accuracy regressions in reranking and increased CPU costs for post-processing. We need a formal adapter + migration playbook that balances correctness, latency, and operator effort.
goals: Define a server-side compatibility adapter that performs deterministic mapping between vector widths (pad/truncate/learned projection) with clear accuracy/latency tradeoffs
Design a staged online reindexing strategy that maintains reranking quality SLOs and allows incremental roll-forward across customer indices
Provide test harnesses and eval thresholds to block migration if reranking NDCG/precision drop exceeds acceptable limits
Document operator runbooks and automated monitoring for rollback and fallback
non_goals: Building a one-size-fits-all learned projection model for every customer (we will prototype for high-value customers only)
Removing the need for full reindex in all cases (some corpora require re-encoding for quality)
API-breaking client changes — aim for backwards-compatible behavior
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility adapter implemented behind feature flag on embeddings service
Automated evaluation harness comparing original vs mapped embeddings on canonical reranking testsets (NDCG@10, MRR) with configurable thresholds
Operator playbook checked into /confluence/embeddings/migration-playbook and a guided Console flow to initiate staged reindex
Latency regression for critical reranking endpoints < 8% p95 after adapter enabled (measured on staging), and cost delta documented
Two pilot customers successfully migrated with rollbacks exercised
implementation_plan: Prototype three adapter strategies: zero-pad/truncate, scaled-truncate, and per-customer linear projection (learned) — evaluate accuracy/latency/cost
Implement adapter as a lightweight middleware in embeddings-access layer; expose mapping type per-index via metadata
Add a 'migration_state' index flag (unmigrated | compat-mapped | reindexed) to control routing and telemetry
Build incremental reindex worker that can copy shards and atomically swap index alias after QA
Create SDK compatibility helpers (Python/Node) that optionally request server-side mapping and validate shape to help client devs
rollout_steps: Day 0: Feature flag deploy to staging with adapter disabled by default
Day 2: Run offline evaluation harness for all impacted model pairs (old->new width) and produce report per customer
Week 1: Enable adapter in staging for internal reranking pipelines and measure NDCG/latency; iterate mapping strategy if >2% NDCG drop
Week 2: Select two low-risk pilot customers, enable adapter in canary region and start background incremental reindex for one
Week 3-6: For each pilot, monitor metrics, complete reindex, run canary traffic for 48h, then mark index as reindexed and disable adapter
Full rollout: Use automation to batch customers by corpus size and observed degradation risk, with ops approval required for >1M docs
testing_and_eval: Create canonical reranking testsets per customer (sampled queries + human judgments where available)
Automated A/B tests comparing current embeddings vs mapped embeddings on staging with NDCG@10 and MRR tracking
Latency microbenchmarks for mapping strategies (per-request CPU/memory and end-to-end p50/p95 impact)
Quality smoke tests that run on every reindex worker job and block swap if quality delta > configured threshold
Unit tests for adapter arithmetic (padding invariants, deterministic projections) and SDK shape checks
monitoring_and_health: Dashboard: migration_overview (customers by migration_state, reindex progress, active adapters)
Per-customer SLO monitor: rerank_quality_change, rerank_latency_pct_change, recent_errors
Alerting: P0 alert if rerank_quality_change < -5% for >30m after adapter enable; P1 for latency p95 > +15%
Audit logs for every mapping operation and index alias swap, retained for 90 days
Automated rollback: mark index alias to fallback variant and notify on-call with runbook link
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Start with deterministic adapters (pad/truncate, scaled truncation) as default; learned projection only for VIP pilot customers due to model management cost
Tradeoff: Zero-padding is cheapest and lowest-latency but can dilute signal for distance metrics; projection preserves geometry better at CPU cost
Decision: Implement adapter in embeddings-access layer (closer to serving) to minimize object shipping and enable per-index metadata checks
Tradeoff: Server-side mapping preserves client compatibility but hides correctness issues until reindex; we will force reindex on a schedule for long-term quality
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Significant NDCG degradation on long-tail customer corpora — Mitigation: require per-customer offline validation and block automated swap if delta > threshold
Risk: Latency increase for high-throughput reranks — Mitigation: benchmark mapping paths, introduce cached mapped-kv for hot prefixes, and use resource-based routing
Risk: Unexpected memory growth on projection models — Mitigation: limit projection model size (per-customer quota) and run OOM safeguards with circuit-breakers
Risk: Customers expect 100% transparent quality — Mitigation: Communicate that adapter is temporary compatibility measure; offer assisted reindex program for critical customers
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created by Asha; initial scoping and list of adapter strategies documented
2026-02-27: Prototype zero-pad and scaled-truncate implemented; offline eval harness scaffolded (Miguel)
2026-03-04: Benchmark results: zero-pad p95 latency +1.2%, scaled-truncate +2.8%; NDCG median drop: zero-pad 1.8%, scaled 0.9%
2026-03-09: Design review with PM and Design — choose default to offer scaled-truncate as default mapping, learned projection gated behind pilot
2026-03-12: Feature-flagged adapter merged to staging; operator playbook draft in Confluence; looking for pilot customers
notes: Recommend offering a migration assistance package for customers with >5M docs; schedule reindex windows to avoid peak traffic
Consider adding an opt-in telemetry flag so customers can consent to server-side mapping for a 30-day trial
Track cost delta per-customer and feed into billing for Dedicated and Private customers differently
